If fainting (Murcha) or hypovolemic shock occurs, administer sweet cardiac stimulants and keep patient in Trendelenburg position.

text: Uttara Basti (intra-urethral and intra-uterine enema) safety guidelines: Strict asepsis is mandatory. Indications: infertility (Vandhyatva), severe dysmenorrhea (Kashta-artava), uterine prolapse, recurrent urinary retention (Mutraghata), and chronic bladder pain. Maximum urethral dose for males: 1/2 Pala (approx 24 ml); for females: 1 Pala (approx 48 ml) for vaginal/uterine instillation. Complications: urinary tract infection, hematuria, acute pelvic colic. Management: urethral wash with lukewarm decoction of Gokshura and Nyagrodha barks; oral administration of Chandanasava.

text: Contraindications for internal oleation (Snehapana): Internal ghee/oil therapy must NEVER be administered to: 1. Patients with acute digestive impairment (Mandagni) or Ama accumulation, 2. Acute poisoning, 8. Alcohol intoxication (Madatyaya), and 9. Pregnancy in early trimesters. Administering Sneha in Ama condition leads to incurable systemic endotoxemia (Amadosha), dermatological obstinacy, and severe cardiometabolic collapse.

section_heading: Chapter 13: Snehadhyaya - Signs of Proper, Deficient, and Excessive Oleation (Samyak, Ayoga, Atiyoga)
text: Clinical criteria for assessing Snehana progress: Samyak Snigdha Lakshana (proper oleation): Vatanulomana (unobstructed downward passage of flatus and feces), Deeptagni (strong appetite), unctuous and loose stools (Snigdha Asamhata Pureesha), softness and unctuousness of skin (Snigdha Gatrata), and aversion to further fat intake (Sneha Udvega). Ayoga Lakshana (under-oleation): Dry hard stools, rough skin, burning digestion, and stiffness. Atiyoga Lakshana (excessive oleation): Pallor (Panduta), heaviness of body, indigestion, drowsiness, nausea, and presence of undigested fat in feces. Management of Atiyoga: fasting (Langhana), dry powders (Ruksha Churna), Triphala decoction, and Takra (buttermilk).

section_heading: Chapter 14: Swedadhyaya - Contraindications and Complications of Sudation (Swedana)
text: Contraindications for Sudation (Swedana Anarha): Swedana must not be administered in: 1. Hemorrhagic disorders (Raktapitta), 2. Severe Pitta constitution or aggravated Pitta, 3. Uncontrolled diabetes (Prameha), 4. Acute diarrhea and dysentery, 5. Severe emaciation (Kshina), 6. Cardiac disease (Hridroga), 7. Extreme dizziness (Bhrama), 8. Blindness or eye inflammation (Timira), 9. Pregnancy (Garbhini), and 10. Testicular and scrotal swelling. In cardiac, ocular, and testicular regions, only extremely mild or no heat may ever be applied. Complications of Atisveda (excessive sudation): fainting (Murcha), thermal burns, extreme thirst, joint flaccidity, and fever. Antidote: cooling baths, sugar water, sweet fruit juices, and application of sandalwood.

section_heading: Section 3: Standard Operating Protocol for Vamana Karma (Therapeutic Emesis)
text: Standard Operating Protocol for Vamana Karma: Pre-procedure (Purva Karma): Internal oleation (Snehapana) with medicated ghee (e.g., Indukanta Ghrita or Mahatiktaka Ghrita) in escalating doses for 3 to 7 days until Samyak Snigdha signs appear, followed by one day of resting diet (Kapha-aggravating meals like curd and black gram) and Abhyanga-Swedana. Procedure day (Pradhana Karma): Confirm morning fasting state. Administer stomach-filling liquid (Akantha-pana) using milk, sugarcane juice, or Yashtimadhu Phanta. Administer Vamana Yoga (Madanaphala Pippali churna 3-6g with Vacha, honey, and Saindhava). Observe Vega (emetic bouts) count: Pravara (8 Vegas), Madhyama (6 Vegas), Avara (4 Vegas). Target termination: Appearance of Pittanta (yellowish bile in vomitus), lightness of chest, and cessation of emetic urge.

section_heading: Section 4: Standard Operating Protocol for Virechana Karma (Therapeutic Purgation)
text: Standard Operating Protocol for Virechana Karma: Indications: Chronic skin disorders (Eczema, Psoriasis), Liver disorders (Jaundice, Hepatitis), Chronic fever, Gouty arthritis (Vatarakta), Chronic hyperacidity (Amlapitta), and Bronchial asthma with Pitta involvement. Pre-procedure: 3-7 days Snehapana, 3 days Sarvanga Abhyanga and Bashpa Sweda, light dinner previous night. Procedure day: Administer Virechana formulation between 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM (after Kapha time subsides). Formulations: Trivrit Leham (15-30g), Ichhabhedi Rasa (125-250mg for severe constipation only), or Castor oil with ginger water. Vega counting: Pravara (30 stools), Madhyama (20 stools), Avara (10 stools). Target end-point: Kaphanta (mucus appearing in final bowel movements), relief of abdomen, normal vital signs.

section_heading: Section 5: Post-Shodhana Graduated Dietary Regimen (Samsarjana Krama)
text: Post-purificatory dietary schedule (Samsarjana Krama) to reignite sluggish digestive fire (Mandagni): 1. Peya (thin clear rice gruel without salt or spices): provides hydration and easy assimilation. 2. Vilepi (thick rice gruel): restores bodily vigor and peristalsis. 3. Akrita Yusha (unseasoned green gram / Mung lentil soup without salt and oil). 4. Krita Yusha (seasoned Mung soup cooked with mild ghee, cumin, and Saindhava salt). 5. Akrita Mamsa Rasa (unseasoned clear meat broth) followed by Krita Mamsa Rasa (seasoned broth) for non-vegetarians, or seasoned pulse soups for vegetarians. Dosing cycles based on Shuddhi grade: Pravara Shuddhi (3 meal sessions each stage, 7 days total); Madhyama Shuddhi (2 meal sessions each stage, 5 days total); Avara Shuddhi (1 meal session each stage, 3 days total). Strict prohibition: Heavy, cold, fried, curd, and sour foods are strictly forbidden during Samsarjana Krama.

section_heading: Section 6: Basti Administration Protocols - Niruha and Anuvasana

Makshika (honey) and Saindhava (rock salt) triturated thoroughly, 2. Sneha (medicated oil/ghee) added and emulsified, 3. Kalka (fine medicinal herbal paste) blended, 4. Kwatha (warm decoction) added gradually, and 5. Avapa (adjuvant liquids) mixed into homogenous emulsion. Patient positioning: Left lateral position (Vama Parshwa) with left leg extended and right leg flexed at hip and knee.

section_heading: Chapter 2: Patient Screening and Informed Consent in Panchakarma
text: Mandatory clinical screening criteria before commencing any Panchakarma procedure: 1. Comprehensive baseline physical examination including recording of Blood Pressure, Resting Heart Rate, Respiratory Rate, Blood Glucose (RBS), ECG for patients above 45 years, and routine urinalysis. 2. Detailed Prakriti and Vikriti assessment to identify doshic predisposition and tolerance thresholds. 3. Verification of patient's current Western pharmacological regimen (e.g., anti-hypertensives, anticoagulants, antiplatelets, insulin, oral hypoglycemics). Patients on Warfarin, Heparin, or Clopidogrel must NOT undergo Raktamokshana or invasive Siravyadha without hematologist clearance. 4. Execution of written informed consent documenting procedure steps, dietary limitations, and recognized potential side effects.

section_heading: Chapter 5: Operational Safety and Infection Control in Jalaukavacharana (Leech Therapy)
text: Operational safety guidelines for Jalaukavacharana (Leech Therapy): 1. Leech selection: Only certified non-poisonous medicinal leeches (Hirudo medicinalis / Nirvisha Jalauka, recognized by green-brown dorsal stripes and active swimming motility) must be used. Never use wild uncertified leeches. 2. Single-patient use: A leech applied to a patient MUST be marked and quarantined or safely discarded according to biomedical waste rules. Never reuse a leech across different patients to eliminate hepatitis B, C, and HIV transmission risks. 3. Host preparation: Clean target skin thoroughly with sterile distilled water; avoid scented soaps, antiseptics, or alcohol immediately before application as leeches will refuse biting. 4. Post-detachment management: Leech is induced to vomit ingested blood using turmeric powder (Haridra Churna). Patient bite site is dusted with sterile Haridra or Shatadhouta Ghrita and sterile pressure dressing applied for 12 hours.

section_heading: Chapter 7: Prevention and Management of Scalds and Thermal Injuries during Swedana
text: Thermal safety protocol during Swedana (steam and bolus sudation): 1. Steam chamber (Bashpa Sweda) safety: Boiler pressure gauges must be calibrated quarterly. Steam temperature entering chamber must not exceed 42°C to 45°C. Patient's head must remain strictly outside the steam chamber with a cold wet towel wrapped on forehead. Continuous verbal communication with patient is mandatory; session terminated immediately upon profuse perspiration on forehead or patient request. Maximum duration: 15 to 20 minutes. 2. Pinda Sweda (Patra Pinda / Shashtika Shali Pinda Sweda): Therapist must test the bolus temperature on the dorsal aspect of their own wrist before touching patient skin. Never apply a boiling bolus directly. 3. First aid for thermal scald: Immediate application of cold water, Aloe vera pulp (Kumari Swarasa), or silver sulfadiazine ointment.

section_heading: Chapter 8: Emergency Management of Vasovagal Syncope and Hypotension in Panchakarma
text: Emergency Management of Vasovagal Syncope and Acute Hypotension during Panchakarma: Trigger factors: Orthostatic repositioning after steam bath, emotional fear during emesis, excessive bowel evacuation, or severe pain. Warning signs: Sudden pallor, cold clammy perspiration, yawning, dizziness, bradycardia, or dropping systolic BP below 90 mmHg. Immediate clinical action: 1. Terminate procedure instantly. 2. Place patient in supine position with legs elevated 30 degrees (Trendelenburg maneuver). 3. Loosen tight garments, ensure fresh airflow, administer high-flow oxygen via nasal cannula. 4. Spray cold water on face. 5. If conscious, administer lukewarm Draksha (raisin) water or glucose solution with a pinch of rock salt. 6. If unconsciousness persists beyond 60 seconds, initiate BLS resuscitation and emergency hospital transfer.

section_heading: Chapter 1: Madanaphala Kalpa - Superiority and Preparation of the Foremost Emetic Drug
text: Madanaphala (Randia dumetorum / Catunaregam spinosa) is declared the foremost and safest among all emetic drugs (Vamaka Dravya) because it produces therapeutic emesis without causing cardiac distress (Anapayi), excessive dehydration, or tissue depletion. Preparation and dosage: Collect ripe, undamaged fruits in spring; extract seeds (Madanaphala Pippali), dry thoroughly, and powder. Standard adult therapeutic dose: 1 Antarnakhamushti (approximately 3 to 6 grams of seed powder), triturated with honey, rock salt (Saindhava), and warm decoction of Yashtimadhu (licorice) or Kovidara. Contraindication: Do not administer raw or fermented fruit pulp as it induces violent gastric spasm and persistent non-therapeutic vomiting.

section_heading: Chapter 2: Jimutaka Kalpa - Indications and Formulations in Febrile and Respiratory Crises

Parshwa-chhidra (side holes instead of terminal orifice): Medicine sprays obliquely against the rectal wall, causing localized trauma. 7. Vakra (bent nozzle): Enema fluid is directed asymmetrically, creating painful rectal spasms. 8. Asamyak-karnika (improper protective ring): Nozzle slips excessively deep into rectum during administration.

text: Yashtimadhu (Glycyrrhiza glabra Linn.) Root Monograph: The premier universal cytoprotective and buffering agent (Madhura-Sheeta, Vranaropana) in Panchakarma practice. Active constituent: Glycyrrhizin, which hydrolyzes to glycyrrhetic acid, stimulating endogenous prostaglandin synthesis, mucus production, and epithelial healing. Standard clinical uses: 1. Vamana Akanthapana: Decoction of Yashtimadhu (Yashtimadhu Phanta) administered up to stomach-filling volume to protect gastric mucosa during emesis and facilitate smooth vomiting bouts without dry retching. 2. Anuvasana and Pichha Basti: Ghee or milk processed with Yashtimadhu to heal anal fissures and reduce tenesmus. 3. Antidote and buffer: Neutralizes the sharpness of Teekshna purgatives like Jayapala and Snuhi. Precaution: Prolonged excessive high-dose use (> 4 weeks) may cause pseudoaldosteronism with sodium retention and hypokalemia.

section_heading: Monograph 12: Saindhava Lavana (Rock Salt) - Emetic Catalyst and Osmotic Mechanism
text: Saindhava Lavana (Rock Salt / Halite Mineral) Monograph: Indispensable catalytic adjuvant in Panchakarma evacuation protocols. Clinical characteristics: Tridoshahara, unctuous, cooling in potency compared to common sea salt (Samudra Lavana), non-irritating to gastric mucosa. Mechanisms of action: 1. In Vamana: Saindhava liquefies thick viscous Kapha (Chedana property) and disrupts adhesion of toxins to gastric mucosal walls. 2. In Niruha Basti: First ingredient triturated with honey (Makshika) to form a stable micro-emulsion with fats; enhances mucosal osmotic absorption and prevents decoction separation. Contraindications: Severe congestive heart failure, acute nephrotic syndrome with severe edema, and malignant hypertension; sea salt must never be substituted for Saindhava in Panchakarma due to higher caustic heat and gastric mucosal irritation risks.

section_heading: Chapter 2: Swedana Vidhi - The Four Classical Categories of Sudation and Clinical Scope
text: Fourfold Classification of Swedana according to Sharngadhara: 1. Tapa Sweda (Direct dry thermal sudation using heated stones, bricks, or metal plates wrapped in cloth): Indicated for localized Vata-Kapha stiffness and pain without acute inflammation. 2. Ushma Sweda (Steam sudation using boiling decoctions or medicinal steam chambers): Indicated for generalized arthritis, hemiplegia, and deep-seated muscular spasms. 3. Upanaha Sweda (Warm medicinal poultices bandaged over joints): Indicated for chronic localized joint contractures, osteoarthritis, and ligament sprains; left in place for 12 hours overnight. 4. Drava Sweda (Liquid sudation including medicated warm baths / Avagaha and streaming showers / Parisheka): Indicated for anorectal fissures, renal colic, dysuria, and acute pelvic pain. Absolute prohibition: Heat must never be applied to the scrotum, cardiac region, or eyes.

section_heading: Chapter 3: Vamana Vidhi - Ingestion Sequence and Prevention of Dry Retching
text: Sharngadhara Operational Sequence for Vamana Administration: 1. Pre-ingestion: Verify prior night light meal and morning empty stomach. Administer Snehana-Swedana 1 hour prior. 2. Akantha-pana (Full stomach filling): Patient drinks milk, sugarcane juice, or warm Yashtimadhu Phanta until throat fullness is reached (Akanthapana). Initiating emesis on a partially filled stomach causes agonizing dry retching (Shushka Udgara), esophageal mucosal tearing, and hematemesis. 3. Drug administration: Madanaphala seed paste mixed with honey and rock salt administered immediately after Akanthapana. 4. Observation: Patient rests quietly for 1 Muhurta (48 minutes); perspiration indicates dosha liquefaction; goosebumps indicate doshas mobilizing toward stomach. 5. Post-emesis care: Wash face with cool water, gargle warm water, inhale mild medicinal smoke (Dhoomapana), and enter rest chamber.

Mild purgatives like Aragvadha will fail, causing abdominal colic and gaseous distension. 2. Mridu Koshtha (Soft, easily evacuative bowel / Pitta predominance): Requires gentle, sweet, cooling laxatives (Mridu Virechana); e.g., Aragvadha fruit pulp, Draksha decoction, or Triphala with warm water. Administering sharp purgatives causes severe uncontrolled diarrhea, hypokalemia, and syncope. 3. Madhyama Koshtha (Moderate bowel / Kapha predominance): Managed with Trivrit root powder (5 to 10 g) with warm water.

section_heading: Chapter 5: Basti Kalpana - The Classical 1:1:2:1:4 Emulsion Ratio for Niruha Basti
text: Sharngadhara's Master Emulsion Ratio for Niruha Basti Preparation (Pancha-Prastha Basti Formula): Proper blending of decoction, fats, and herbal paste is mandatory to prevent chemical separation and severe rectal mucosal irritation. Volumetric mixing ratio: 1. Makshika (Pure Honey): 1 part (approx 100 ml), 2. Saindhava (Rock Salt): 1 part (approx 10 to 15 grams), 3. Sneha (Medicated Oil or Ghee): 2 parts (approx 200 ml), 4. Kalka (Fine medicinal herbal paste): 1 part (approx 50 to 100 grams), 5. Kwatha (Warm strained decoction): 4 parts (approx 400 to 500 ml). Total volume for robust adult: approximately 800 to 960 ml (1 Prastha). Mixing protocol: Triturate Honey and Salt first in a mortar until dissolved; add Sneha gradually while whisking to form a homogenous emulsion; incorporate Kalka paste; lastly stir in warm Kwatha decoction and strain through sterile gauze before administration.

text: Anuvasana Basti and Matra Basti Operational Parameters: Dosing: - Sneha Basti (standard oleating enema): 6 Palas (approx 240 ml). - Anuvasana Basti (moderate oleating enema): 3 Palas (approx 120 ml). - Matra Basti (low-dose retention enema): 1.5 Palas (approx 60 ml). Administration time: Always administer after a warm light meal (Prabhukta Anna) to prevent oil from migrating upward into empty stomach. Expected retention duration: Optimum retention time is 3 Yamas (approx 9 hours). If oil is expelled immediately within 1 hour, therapeutic action is diminished; if retained beyond 24 hours, administer a mild carminative decoction or rectal suppository (Varti) to clear sluggish oil. Safety advantages of Matra Basti: Requires no strict fasting, produces no physical exhaustion, and is safe for daily administration across all ages.

section_heading: Chapter 8: Dhoomapana Vidhi - Medicated Smoke and Management of Accidental Inhalation Complications
text: Operational Guidelines for Medicated Inhalation (Dhoomapana Vidhi): Indications: Post-Vamana and post-Nasya therapy to clear residual Kapha mucus from bronchial passages, throat, and cranial cavities. Three clinical types: Prayogika (daily balancing smoke), Snigdha (lubricating smoke for Vata dry cough), and Vairechanika (purging smoke for heavy sinusitis and headaches). Route rules: Inhale through mouth and exhale through mouth for chest disorders; inhale through nose and ALWAYS exhale through mouth for cranial and sinus conditions. Never exhale smoke through nostrils as heated smoke irritates optic nerves and causes visual impairment (Drishti-Vighata). Complications of excessive smoke: Blindness, deafness, epistaxis, dizziness, and respiratory stridor. Antidote for excessive Dhoomapana: Cold milk eye drops, cold nasal instillation of ghee, and drinking sweet grape juice (Draksha).

text: Sharngadhara Operational Protocols for Oral Retention (Gandusha) and Gargling (Kavala): 1. Gandusha (Static oral fluid retention): Mouth is filled completely with medicated fluid (oil, milk, or decoction) until cheeks are fully stretched and movement of liquid is impossible; held until secretions flow from eyes and nose (Kapha-Pitta elimination endpoint). Four types: Snigdha (with sesame oil/ghee for dry mouth and tooth mobility), Shamana (cooling decoctions for stomatitis and ulcers), Shodhana (with rock salt and vinegar for heavy coated tongue), and Ropana (with astringent barks for oral lacerations). 2. Kavala (Dynamic gargling): Liquid fills half the oral cavity, permitting vigorous swirling and gargling. Contraindications: Inability to swallow, acute unconsciousness, poisoning, and children below 5 years (aspiration danger).

text: The Eight Prohibited Lifestyle and Physical Factors during Panchakarma Rehabilitation (Ashta Mahadoshakara Bhava / Pariharya Vishaya): Following Shodhana, the patient's digestive fire (Agni) and bodily tissues resemble an unbaked earthen pot, highly vulnerable to trauma. section_heading: Section 8: Clinical Monitoring and Thresholds for Inpatient Panchakarma Admissions
text: Mandatory Vital Signs and Biochemical Monitoring Thresholds for Inpatient Panchakarma: 1. Blood Pressure: Systolic BP must remain between 100 and 150 mmHg, Diastolic BP between 65 and 90 mmHg. If Systolic BP drops below 90 mmHg or Diastolic drops below 60 mmHg during emesis or purgation, immediately halt procedure and initiate IV fluid resuscitation (Normal Saline or Ringer's Lactate). 2. Heart Rate: Pulse rate must be recorded every 15 minutes during Pradhana Karma. Bradycardia (< 55 bpm) or severe tachycardia (> 120 bpm) requires immediate medical officer evaluation and 12-lead ECG. 3. Serum Electrolytes: In patients undergoing high-grade Shuddhi (> 20 bouts in Virechana or > 6 bouts in Vamana), post-procedure serum potassium and sodium must be monitored. Potassium levels below 3.5 mEq/L mandate immediate oral potassium citrate or coconut water rehydration to prevent fatal cardiac arrhythmias.

section_heading: Chapter 9: Emergency Management of Acute Anaphylaxis and Drug Allergies
text: Emergency Management of Drug Hypersensitivity and Anaphylactoid Reactions during Panchakarma: Etiology: Hypersensitivity to sulfur-based herbomineral formulations, fermented decoctions (Asava/Arishta), or foreign proteins in leeches. Early warning signs: Generalized urticaria, pruritus, periorbital edema, tightness in chest, and inspiratory stridor. Immediate emergency intervention: 1. Discontinue offending medication immediately. 2. Maintain patent airway; administer oxygen at 6 to 8 L/min via face mask. 3. Intramuscular administration of Epinephrine (Adrenaline 1:1000) 0.5 mg in anterolateral thigh in severe anaphylaxis with airway compromise. 4. Supportive classical administration: Haridra Khanda (5g) with lukewarm water for mild urticarial rashes; Shatadhouta Ghrita for topical erythema. 5. Mandatory documentation in hospital incident register and formal notification to Regional Pharmacovigilance Centre.

section_heading: Chapter 10: Infection Control and Waste Disposal Standards in Panchakarma Centers
text: Infection Control and Biomedical Waste Disposal Protocol for Panchakarma Units: 1. Droni (Treatment table) disinfection: Wooden and fiber Dronis must be wiped thoroughly with neutral hospital disinfectant (0.5% sodium hypochlorite or chlorhexidine-cetrimide solution) between successive patients; never allow oil residues to pool, preventing slip hazards and fungal biofilm growth. 2. Linen management: All sheets, loin cloths (Koupina), and towels must be autoclaved or laundered at > 70°C. 3. Sharp disposal: Scalpels, lancets, and Siravyadha needles must be discarded immediately into puncture-proof red and blue biomedical waste bins; never recap needles manually. 4. Biological waste: Blood-soaked dressings, vomitus collection, and used leeches must be handled as infectious category waste and incinerated or disposed of through authorized biomedical waste handlers.

section_heading: Chapter 11: Emergency Protocols for Acute Aspiration during Vamana Karma
text: Emergency Management of Tracheobronchial Aspiration during Therapeutic Emesis (Vamana): High-risk presentation: Sudden coughing paroxysm, cyanosis of lips, stridor, and tachypnea while vomiting stomach contents. Immediate emergency action: 1. Immediately cease all oral fluid intake. 2. Support patient's forehead and tilt head downward and forward over emesis basin; perform gentle back blows between scapulae to dislodge fluid. 3. Clear oral cavity and oropharynx with mechanical suction catheter; ensure patient does not swallow vomitus back. 4. Administer high-flow humidified oxygen via non-rebreather mask. 5. Inhale warm medicated vapor of Haridra (turmeric) or mild Dhoomapana to relieve laryngeal reflex spasm. 6. If respiratory distress or wheezing persists, auscultate chest for coarse crackles, secure intravenous line, and transfer immediately to ICU for bronchoscopic evaluation and aspiration pneumonitis prophylaxis.

section_heading: Chapter 3: Shirodhara Safety Protocol and Prevention of Chilling and Conjunctivitis
text: Operational Safety and Eye Protection in Shirodhara (Continuous Cranial Oil Pouring): Common complications: Oil trickling into eyes causing acute chemical conjunctivitis; facial chilling and sinusitis from room drafts; hypotensive bradycardia from excessive parasympathetic stimulation. Safety protocol: 1. Eye protection: Place sterile cotton gauze soaked in cold rose water (Gulab Jala) or Triphala decoction over patient's closed eyes and bind with a secure forehead headband to form a mechanical barrier preventing oil entry into conjunctival sac. 2. Oil temperature control: Oil must be maintained continuously at physiological body temperature (37°C to 38°C); therapist must test temperature on wrist before pouring. Cool oil causes acute sinus headache (Shirashoola) and neck stiffness. 3. Pouring height: Shirodhara pot nozzle must be suspended exactly 4 Angulas (approx 8 to 10 cm) above patient's forehead; higher streams cause mechanical intracranial discomfort and headache.

Therapist must reheat replaced oil in a water bath (double boiler); direct open-flame heating of oil is strictly prohibited due to hot spots and burning risks. 3. Oil exchange: Oil must be removed gently with cotton sponge and replaced slowly along inner side of dough ring, never poured directly onto bare spine.
